neighbours.label: the verb after 'to' following an eagerness or pleasure predicate ('eager to work', 'proud to be')
fire: After a long search, our school is delighted to work with a local artist this spring.
The new interns said they were thrilled to work alongside the senior engineers.
As a veteran, he is honored to be part of the parade this year.
Our charity is glad to work with any family that needs help.
The band said it was excited to be back on stage after two years.
Many volunteers were keen to work on the river cleanup.
Each winner was overjoyed to be invited to the ceremony in the capital.
The mayor said she was eager to work with the new council.
quiet: After a long search, our school will have to work with a local artist this spring.
The new interns took the train to work alongside the senior engineers.
As a veteran, he used to be part of the parade every year.
Our charity has to work with any family that is referred to it.
The band said it was about to be back on stage after two years.
Many volunteers walked to work on the day of the river cleanup.
Each winner was going to be invited to the ceremony in the capital.
The mayor said she would need to work with the new council.

predictions: Fire on 'work'/'be' after glad/eager/excited/proud to; near misses use the same verbs after obligation, motion or future 'to'.
notes: Card: ' work' x7, ' be' x7, mostly 'happy/eager/pleased to work/be'. Probe: 'eager to work' 0.700, 'excited to work' 0.567, 'proud to be' 0.527, 'happy to help' 0.249; 'need to work' 0.137, 'went to work' 0.230, 'going to be' 0.079. Max is small (4.3) so scores are noisy.
